sources.title: Original fence, finite differences, forward hooks and raw-measurement recomputation
Original completed optimizer update counter inspection

claims.statement: top-k chooses k experts per token; independent stored expert sets remain available while unselected experts can be skipped for that token. Computing all experts first and discarding outputs does not save their expert computation.
claims.scope: Equal-architecture independent expert storage and expert-side conditional computation. Does not promise end-to-end speed, equal FLOPs or expert specialization. The noisy gate and normalization of Shazeer2017 are not conflated with this raw-probability demonstration.

evidence.locator: p2 section1.2 and Figure1; p3 section1.2 continuation and section2 equation1/computation paragraph; p4 section2.1 equations3-5
evidence.supports: Separate expert parameters, a potentially different selection at each text position, and no need to evaluate E_i(x) for zero gate. Top-k restricts the active combination per input.

claims.statement: The original two-row, three-column fence selects largest k entries along the expert axis and returns sorted values plus original integer column indices without normalization or expert execution; displayed sums and both exercises are correct. Tied indices need not be stable.
claims.location: course/chapters/15.md original fence lines126-133 and paragraphs136,142
claims.scope: Grouped API coverage: torch.tensor, Tensor.topk(k,dim=-1), Tensor.sum(-1), Tensor.tolist, topk defaults/tie contract; exact integer choices for distinct input values, float32 value/sum tolerance1e-7. Fence has no backward, expert call or parameter update. Binary approximation principle applies, without treating Python float53-bit examples as tensor dtype claims. No cross-device tie behavior was measured.

evidence.supports: Construction, reduction on the requested axis, largest/sorted defaults, returned values/indices and documented unstable tied indices.
Method contracts and conversion to nested ordinary Python lists.
Finite binary representations approximate many decimal fractions; display may expose nearby decimals.
Unchanged original fence executed; row swap and k3 independently checked with numerical tolerance.

verification.expected: k2 indices[[1,2],[0,1]], sums[.9,.9]; k1 indices[[1],[0]], sums[.7,.6]; first-row swap gives[2,1] and[.7,.2]; k3 retains all three with sum1.
verification.observed: All assertions pass; actual float32 sums .8999999761581421/.9000000357627869 and .699999988079071/.6000000238418579; row-swap and k3 match.
verification.details: Executed the original280-byte fence without modifications, then bounded CPU variants. Values, axes, shape(2,k), integer indices and no normalization checked together.
verification.tolerance: Integer indices exact for distinct values; float32 absolute tolerance1e-7, zero relative tolerance.

claims.statement: The expert identity is an integer choice that changes at ranking boundaries; ordinary autograd does not differentiate those indices. Retained softmax values can propagate a local gradient to router scores while the chosen set stays fixed.
claims.scope: Local selected-value derivative away from ties and ranking boundaries, with the current unnormalized probability convention. Does not assert nonzero gradients for every loss, or normalized top1; does not prove a trained router learned useful choices.

evidence.supports: topk values are differentiable, indices are not; the backward routes selected value gradients.

evidence.locator: p4 section2.1 Training the Gating Network and preceding discontinuity paragraph
evidence.supports: Original sparse gate can have discontinuities at selection changes while selected continuous gates permit backpropagation; original normalized k>1 condition remains distinct.
k1 and k2 raw retained softmax weighted sums have autograd gradients matching fixed-set finite differences; crossing the rank boundary switches indices.

claims.statement: The repository MoEFFN actually chooses before dispatch and only calls an expert on its selected token rows. A token can select different experts from another token in the same batch.
claims.location: course/chapters/15.md lines121,123,140; linked actual implementation tiny_perceptron/modern.py56-84
claims.scope: Implementation inspection plus a two-token/four-expert CPU forward-hook probe. Verifies input-row work and skipped unselected experts; gives no training, GPU performance or wall-time improvement claim.

evidence.supports: topk precedes expert evaluation; token_rows/slots from chosen==i, conditional execution, weighted contributions and row restoration.
Controlled router choices produce2 expert input rows for top1 and4 for top2, compared with8 if every expert processed both tokens; fourth expert never called.

verification.expected: top1 chosen[[1],[0]], rows[1,1,0,0]; top2 chosen[[1,2],[0,1]], rows[1,2,1,0]; output shape[2,2].
verification.observed: Forward pre-hooks show the expected selected rows and zero calls for unselected experts, including expert3 in both cases. Output shape preserved.
verification.details: Actual imported MoEFFN;4 experts, width2, hidden3, controlled router matrix. CPU/eval/no_grad, no optimizer and no parameter update. Source SHA agrees with original recorded implementation.

claims.statement: The existing original two-layer/four-expert validation routing has39256 effective input positions after excluding padding. Each layer has39256 top1 assignments or78512 top2 assignments; expert shares use that layer valid-input-count times k denominator.
claims.scope: Original saved measurements for top1_aux0, top1_aux0.01, top2_aux0 and top2_aux0.01, both layers each. CPU reconstruction of data denominator and recorded shares only; padding exclusion concerns statistics, not all model computation. No model weights loaded, no training, no GPU re-evaluation, no architecture-quality or speed conclusion. Original experiment Python3.13.3/torch2.14.1+cu126 differs from reviewer Python3.13.5/torch2.14.1+cpu.

evidence.locator: /results/variants/{top1_aux0,top1_aux0.01,top2_aux0,top2_aux0.01}/validation_routing/{effective_input_tokens,padding_excluded,layers/{0,1}/{dispatch_counts,dispatch_denominator,load_fraction}}; matching model/config and dataset/validation; original provenance pointers listed in verification-results.json
evidence.supports: Full raw counts, layer separation, declared effective-input count and per-layer shares in the original saved experiment.

evidence.locator: _routing380-427; original revision48a4f3e... _routing byte-equality with current; run_moe430-441,456-476
evidence.supports: Hooks filter chosen with current_valid, count chosen.flatten, and divide count by count.sum; every layer maintained separately, input denominator accumulated once.
Two-layer default, original seed42 family split, exact validation fingerprint and bounded chunk construction.
Boolean valid mask marks actual inputs and excludes right-side PAD in measurement.
Actual preserved validation data content supports independent effective-position reconstruction.
All four variants, both layers, count sums and shares recalculated; raw data split fingerprint matches, effective mask sum39256.
Original completed short-training counters180 requested/attempted/optimizer updates, no skipped updates; no new training run.

verification.expected: Each of8 layer records has4 integer counts, sum39256*k and matching fractions; same seed42 validation dataset fingerprint and39256 valid positions.
verification.observed: All counts exactly sum39256(top1) or78512(top2); every reconstructed share exactly matches recorded float values.51 validation records produce334 chunks,42752 padded positions minus3496 PAD =39256 valid positions.
verification.details: Named original JSON pointers only, no notes/outcome interpretations. Historical source full SHA matches recorded code hash; _routing itself identical to current. Dataset reconstructed from existing raw input; no training/model download or evaluation.

tool_limits: Chromium original and bounded retry plus blank-page smoke all timed out; no desktop/mobile page image was produced or viewed. Their failure logs are preserved. There is no manuscript figure to leave technically unverified. No deployed-site layout acceptance is claimed.

factual_accuracy.details: Independently checked per-token sparse routing, actual execution path, topk API/example outputs, integer/continuous gradient distinction and original measurement denominator. No substantive unknown remains.

numeric_verification.details: Original float32 fence and exercise variants execute unchanged with1e-7 tolerance; retained-value float64 finite differences differ by at most1.87e-11. All8 layer count sums and shares independently recomputed, and raw-data validation denominator reconstructed exactly.

figure_consistency.details: 15.4 references no manuscript figure. Original paper Figure1 was actually rendered via Inkscape and personally viewed. Chromium section-page desktop/mobile render failed with saved timeouts; no deployed-site/layout visual acceptance claimed.

source_verification.details: Personally read original Shazeer2017v1 title/version and relevant paragraphs/equations, pinned official PyTorch docs/derivative source equal to installed git hash, CPython v3.13.5 docs, actual repository method nodes and named original raw counters. Locator indexes used only to locate originals.

limitations.details: Example is selection only; gradient probe has no optimizer; sparse forward hooks support expert work skipping without runtime claims. Original data/counter verification is not new training or model evaluation, and per-layer PAD-excluded statistics do not imply padding was skipped by every FFN. No sparse routing speed/quality advantage or expert specialization is asserted. Browser render failure retained as a tool limitation for this no-figure section.
